subject: Secure SDLC evidence — itemized artifacts & walkthrough
messages:
From: Clara Hughes <clara.hughes@secureassessors.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@clearedgecapital.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: artifacts for SDLC control assessment (code review, CI/CD, secrets)

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for making time on short notice. As part of ClearEdge's upcoming SIG/SOC2 intake we need a short, itemized package showing your Secure SDLC controls. To keep the assessor runbook tight, could you provide the following by Friday 3/5 if possible:

- High-level description of code review policy and a sample PR review demonstrating reviewer comments and merge approvals (redacted where needed).
- CI/CD controls: pipeline definition (YAML), sample build+deploy logs for a recent release, and any automatic gating/approval steps.
- Secrets management: key custody (who holds KMS roles), rotation cadence, and an example of an access request and approval ticket.
- Change management: a short chronology of a recent change (ticket id, approvers, deploy times) and how rollbacks are authorized.

If you can share redacted artifacts (PDF/text/CSV) and a shared Drive link we can start the review. Also would like to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough the week of 3/8 to talk through the artifacts and run a quick demo of the pipeline.

Two practical notes: we only need enough detail to validate controls (no source dump), and redactions for sensitive customer data are fine.

Best,
Clara

--
Clara Hughes
Senior Assessor, SecureAssessors Ltd.

Hi Clara — thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble an itemized package and can hit the 3/5 target; thanks for the heads-up on redaction scope.

Quick plan:
- Jordan will pull a redacted PR thread and a brief narrative of our review policy.
- Irene will collect CI/CD pipeline YAML, a short set of build logs (redacted), and notes on gating.
- Marissa will extract a recent change chronology and the change authorization trail.
- I'll produce a short KMS/access roles CSV with role names redacted and link to the key rotation policy.

I've uploaded initial artifacts to a Drive folder (link below) and attached the current SDLC runbook plus a CI logs sample for your intake. We'll continue to add items over the day.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3C-sdlc-evidence-cedge
Attachments: sdlc-runbook-v2.pdf; ci-pipeline-sample-logs.txt; kms-access-roles-redacted.csv

Would you prefer the 30-minute walkthrough on 3/9 or 3/10 (PST)? We can do a short live demo of the pipeline; if your team can't attend live we'll record the demo.

Regards,

Thanks — I'm pulling the PR thread now. A couple of clarifications for the assessor:

- Which CI logs are acceptable? I'll include the build+deploy logs from the canary run on 2027-02-18 and redact IPs and customer identifiers. The larger ingest logs are sensitive so we'll avoid those.
- For code review, do you need a full PR diff or just the review thread (comments + approvals)? We can provide the review thread (exported as PDF) plus the PR checklist we enforce at merge.

Attachment: change-log-snapshot-202702.zip (contains ticket chronologies and release timestamps; all PII redacted).

Hannah — dropping the redacted KMS role map and a short note on rotation cadence.

Summary (in the forwarded doc):
- Root KMS keys are in a hardened account; access requires two-step approval from SecOps + Eng manager for emergency use.
- Key rotation: monthly automatic rotation for data-encryption keys; CMK rotations annually with ticketed approval.
- Access requests: we keep a ticket + approval artifact in Jira, and we include the approval header in the KMS audit record export (sample attached).

Attachments: kms-access-roles-redacted.csv

Irene Choi\Principal Engineer, Infrastructure Security

Hannah — this is great, thanks to you and the team for the quick turnaround. I've downloaded the runbook and the redacted artifacts and they look coherent. A few small follow-ups before the walkthrough:

- For the PR example, the review thread and checklist PDF will be sufficient; no need for a full diff.
- For CI/CD, the canary build logs you mentioned plus a short video (5–7 minutes) showing the deploy gate would be very helpful. If you can record a quick screen capture of the pipeline dashboard and share the recording link before the meeting, that will speed our review.
- For KMS: the redacted CSV and the two-step approval description are fine; we may ask for a short snippet of the audit export (redacted) during the call.

Schedule: 3/9 at 10:00 AM PST works for our assessor team. Please send a calendar invite. If anything changes we can push to 3/10.

Best,
Clara
